actions.action: Became a full Tailwind v4 project in its own right: added package.json (tailwindcss + @tailwindcss/typography + @tailwindcss/cli, matching the parent's versions), assets/css/src/site-theme.css (the entire design-token system moved verbatim from the parent theme's own assets/css/src/site-theme.css -- @theme block, @layer base, @layer components with every .hex-*/.btn/.card/.form-control/.table-styled/.alert/.badge/.nav-menu/.nav-link/.accordion/.tabs/.icon/.prose-override class), and assets/css/src/front.css (imports tailwindcss's theme+utilities layers only -- deliberately skips a second Preflight, already provided by the parent's own build -- plus the typography plugin and ./site-theme.css; @source directives scan the PARENT theme's PHP templates across the sibling directory, since the actual page markup still lives there, confirmed working by finding max-w-6xl -- a utility used in the parent's header.php -- correctly compiled into this theme's own output). Ran a real `npm install` (network available, verified via `npm ping` first) and `npm run build:css`, producing assets/css/tailwind.css. Updated functions.php to enqueue that compiled file (new 'hexnity-wp-child-tailwind' handle, depending on the parent's 'hex-tailwind') before this theme's own style.css. Updated style.css's own comment (previously described the parent as the real styling source; now describes this theme's own build as the source) and bumped Version 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0 in style.css and HEXNITY_WP_CHILD_VERSION in functions.php together. Added .gitignore (/node_modules/) matching the parent theme's own convention (compiled CSS committed, node_modules not). Verified live on http://mindlabz-new.local/: hexnity-wp-child/assets/css/tailwind.css loads correctly in the page's <link> tags, and .entry-title's fluid H2 font-size still computed exactly 74.8333px -- unchanged visually, confirming the move didn't break anything. The parent theme's own compiled CSS was correspondingly stripped of all these classes (see the parent's own action-map.json for that side) -- this theme is now the sole source of the design-system's CSS rules; the parent theme alone (no child theme active) renders with zero component styling, an explicit, confirmed trade-off.

actions.user_requirement: Full audit of both themes requested from the main theme's session ("confirm everything industry standed and connected each other"). This theme's own record of the same action.
actions.action: Live-verified (browser, mindlabz-new.local, this theme active) that this theme's style.css was being loaded via two separate <link> tags -- once via the parent theme's own 'hex-style' handle, once via this theme's own 'hexnity-wp-child-style' handle. Tried removing the duplicate by dequeuing+deregistering 'hex-style' inside hexnity_wp_child_enqueue_assets() -- this broke the live site (hex-style/hex-animate/hex-tailwind all stopped rendering, since hex-animate and hex-tailwind both declare 'hex-style' as a WP style dependency and deregistering it broke resolution for all three). Reverted immediately, re-verified live all 5 stylesheets returned, and left the duplicate in place as documented, accepted, low-severity behavior (see ../hex-wp-theme-template/knoladge/child-theme-css-token-architecture.md for the full writeup) -- it's a harmless second <link> tag to an already-cached URL, not a functional defect, and the load-order it provides is what lets a one-off override rule in this theme's style.css win against a Tailwind class. Added an explanatory comment to functions.php recording why 'hex-style' must not be deregistered from here. Bumped version 1.2.0 -> 1.2.1 in style.css and functions.php.
